findings.explanation: This contradicts dataSources ('The TA does not expose actual cloud-archive utilisation') and the SPL, which only counts configuration-change events. Meraki Cloud Archive retention is set by license duration (7/30/90/180/365 days), not storage capacity, so there is no usage figure to track.
findings.quote: Tracks cloud storage usage for video archives to manage costs and ensure retention SLA.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the search as an audit of who changed camera quality, retention or recording-schedule settings, on which network, and when. State that cloud-archive capacity is not measurable from the TA.

findings.explanation: The SPL returns change counts and last-change time per adminEmail, networkName, page and label. It has no storage metric, so a gauge or storage trend cannot be built from it.
findings.quote: Storage utilization gauge; retention timeline; storage trend chart.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a table of recent retention or quality changes (admin, network, page, label, oldValue → newValue, time) and a timeline of change events.

findings.explanation: The Meraki webhook sample-alert catalogue has no 'Camera storage' alert type. The camera alerts listed are 'Motion detected', 'Potential Cloud Archive Issue' (cloud_archive_alert) and 'Camera may have critical hardware failure'.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the alert list in Network-wide > Alerts, or GET /organizations/{organizationId}/webhooks/alertTypes. Replace the name with the real alert, probably 'Potential Cloud Archive Issue' (alertTypeId cloud_archive_alert). Apply the same fix in implementation and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: The Meraki add-on is Splunkbase 5580 (Splunk_TA_cisco_meraki). splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5631 returns 404 and is not in the cached catalogue. This reference sends readers to a wrong or dead listing.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 5631 reference. Keep the 5580 entry with its real title, 'Cisco Meraki Add-on for Splunk'.

findings.explanation: This is a generic Cisco Security support index, unrelated to Meraki MV or the audit endpoint. The 5580 entry is titled only 'Splunkbase app 5580'.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these with the Meraki add-on documentation, the Meraki getOrganizationConfigurationChanges API page and the MV Cloud Archive article.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The title promises 'Cloud Archive Storage Utilization', but the SPL only audits configuration changes to camera quality, retention and schedule settings. Cloud Archive is duration-licensed, so it has no utilisation to measure. Retitle to something like 'Camera Video Retention Setting Changes (Meraki MV)'.

The `like(label, "%schedule%")` and `like(page, "%camera%")` filters are loose and case-sensitive. '%schedule%' also matches non-camera schedule changes (SSID or port schedules), and capitalised page names such as 'Camera...' would miss '%camera%'. Check the real `page` and `label` values in meraki:audit for camera retention changes, and match case-insensitively (for example with lower()).
The search detects configuration changes, not performance, so 'Performance' does not fit. A configuration or change-tracking type fits better.

summary: The title, visualization and detailedImplementation promise cloud-archive storage utilisation. The SPL and dataSources admit that only camera quality-and-retention configuration changes from the audit log are tracked. Meraki Cloud Archive is licensed by retention duration, not by capacity, so a 'utilisation' framing is misleading, and one reference points at a non-existent Splunkbase ID.
